skill.name: skill-management
skill.description: Safely list, inspect, create, revise, and delete agent skill definitions.
skill.purpose: Manage skill definitions without executing their workflows. Preserve existing skill behavior during revisions, delegate natural-language creation to `skill-bootstrap`, and protect against accidental destructive changes.
skill.scope: - Valid modules: `finance`, `obsidian`, and `configuration`. - A skill-management request changes only the selected skill definition; never execute the selected skill's downstream tools. - Resolve an agent id to its configured module before operating on its skills.
skill.intent_routing:
1. LIST (list, view, inspect, show): - Call `list_skills(module)` only. - Never chain create, edit, or delete tools after a list intent. - Return each skill's name and description, plus the module searched.
2. PREVIEW (preview, read, open, inspect content, show skill): - Call `preview_skill(module, name)` only. - Return the full skill file content to the user. - Never execute the skill steps or call downstream agent tools after a preview.
3. CREATE (create, add, new): - Delegate to `skill-bootstrap` from attached skills or call `read_skill("skill-bootstrap")`. - Follow its single-prompt workflow: discover context, generate the complete definition, and create it in the same turn. - Do not manually request a name, description, or body when the user provides a natural-language goal. - If the user supplies a complete module, name, description, and body, validate the module and name collision, then call `create_skill(module, name, description, content)`. - The create tool sets the root `skill` module attribute from the module argument.
4. EDIT (edit, update, change, rewrite): - Call `preview_skill(module, name)` first. - Preserve unchanged valid sections; do not replace the entire behavior with a partial user instruction. - Validate referenced tools, paths, schemas, and attachments against the selected agent before writing. - Call `edit_skill(module, name, description, content)` with the full replacement description and body. - Report the changed behavior and any inferred defaults.
5. DELETE (remove, delete): - Require explicit confirmation that identifies the skill name and module before deleting. - Call `delete_skill(module, name, confirmToken)` with confirmToken equal to `delete-skill:{module}:{name}`. - Report the deletion only after the tool succeeds.
skill.resolution_rules: - If the module is missing, infer it only when the target agent or workflow makes ownership unambiguous; otherwise ask one focused question. - If a skill name is missing for preview, edit, or delete, list the target module's skills and ask the user to select one. - For create or edit, reject invalid XML, a duplicate name, or references to unavailable capabilities before writing. - Skill names must be concise kebab-case identifiers. Descriptions must be precise, one-line catalog summaries.
skill.write_safety: - Never create, edit, or delete a skill after a list or preview-only request. - Never overwrite a similarly named existing skill during CREATE; use EDIT only with user authorization. - Never delete a skill based solely on an ambiguous reference, a list response, or an inferred name. - Preserve XML validity and omit the root `skill` element from `create_skill` and `edit_skill` body content.

output_contract.preview_result: Module: [module] Skill Name: [name] Status: Previewed Content: [full skill definition]
output_contract.write_result: Module: [module] Skill Name: [name] Status: [Created | Updated | Deleted] Summary: [concise outcome] Assumptions: [inferred defaults or "None"]
